I could not run a Monte Carlo code, so this sample is constructed by hand from approximate physics rather than drawn at random from a simulation. The process fractions, energy split and Compton kinematics are approximate, so treat it as illustrative.

For 1.17 and 1.33 MeV in water, Compton scattering dominates (about 99% of interactions), pair production is about 0.5%, Rayleigh about 0.2%, and photoelectric is negligible. At 5 cm depth in a 10 × 10 cm field I assumed roughly 70% primary and 30% scattered photons among interactions. The 200 events are: 138 primary Compton (69 per line), 60 scattered Compton (0.2–0.7 MeV), 1 Rayleigh and 1 pair. Compton outgoing energies, electron energies and electron angles follow Klein-Nishina kinematics for the listed scattering angles.
